understanding.purpose: スタンダードとプレミアムの製品仕様を項目別に比較し、備考で補足する表。
understanding.reading: 左端で仕様項目を見つけ、同じ行の両モデルを横に比較してから備考を読む。行ごとのまとまりと、2つのモデル列の対等さが重要。
groups: スタンダードとプレミアムは同じ仕様を比較する列なので、同幅にして対応を見やすくする。
項目と備考は比較の手がかりと補足を担い、内容に応じて幅を変えられる。
keep_intact: 180 g・195 gなどの数値と単位
20 時間・32 時間などの数値と単位
本体サイズの各数値と単位
may_wrap: 本体サイズの寸法は区切り記号の位置で折り返せる。
備考の説明文は自然な位置で折り返せる。
項目名やモデル名も必要に応じて折り返せるが、比較の見やすさを損なわない幅が望ましい。
寸法や備考が複数行になる行では、同じ行の他のセルの折り返しをその行高に収められる。

bad.why: The narrow item and notes columns fragment labels and prose into many short lines. The long notes dominate the row heights while the product columns contain substantial empty space.
The notes column forces prose into up to seven short lines, making the final rows disproportionately tall and difficult to scan across.
The narrow product columns break both dimension values over three lines and leave the unit g alone on a line, weakening comparison of the two products.

final.rationale: r3A gives the two product columns equal width, so corresponding specifications align and can be compared easily. Its wider notes column keeps the two longest explanations to four lines, while dimensions remain on two lines in both product columns. The item labels wrap, but remain recognizable and close to the values they identify.

general: Give columns with the same comparative role consistent widths when their content permits it.
Allocate width to long prose where it improves reading across the whole row, while preserving meaningful units and comparable values.
specific: Here, the notes column needs more room than either product column because it contains full explanatory sentences.
At 85px, each product column holds the dimensions in two lines; narrower examples wrap them to three.

final.tradeoffs: r2B gives the item labels slightly more room, but leaves the final note on five lines. r3B gives notes a little more width, at the cost of a third line for both dimension values.
final.uncertain: A designer might accept r3B for its wider item and notes columns, depending on how much weight they place on compact dimension values. The stated ranges are conservative: only the preferred widths are verified as equally good by the supplied renders; nearby widths could also work.

A.why: The product columns are balanced and easy to compare, but the narrow notes column creates many short lines and tall rows. Several labels and both product headers wrap.

B.why: The notes column is especially narrow, breaking phrases into short fragments and making the last two rows very tall. The product columns remain balanced.

C.why: The wider notes column makes the long explanations much easier to read, and the product columns remain equal. The narrow item column breaks labels heavily, while dimensions need three lines.

D.why: The product names and dimensions have more room, but the notes are squeezed into very short lines and the item labels also break heavily. The final row becomes particularly tall.

E.why: Balanced product columns support comparison, but the notes wrap into many short lines and make the last two rows tall. Item labels and product headers also wrap.

F.why: The notes have enough room for more natural phrases, while the equal product columns keep specifications aligned for comparison. Some labels and both product headers still wrap.

reviews.unsure: C gives the notes more room, but its narrower item and product columns cause more wrapping. F offers the better overall balance, though that trade-off is close.

A.why: The two product columns are equal and their values align for comparison. Labels and notes wrap, but remain reasonably readable.

B.why: The product columns stay equal, and the wider notes column reduces wrapping. Some row labels and both product headers still split.

C.why: The narrow notes column breaks sentences into many short lines, making the last two rows tall and difficult to scan.

D.why: The notes read comfortably, but narrow label and product columns fragment row names, headers and dimensions, weakening comparisons.

E.why: The narrow label and notes columns create excessive wrapping, while the unequal treatment of the two product headers weakens their shared hierarchy.

F.why: Balanced product columns make comparisons straightforward, though labels, headers and notes wrap across several lines.

reviews.unsure: A and F are visually close to B; the preference depends on how much weight to give the shorter notes against slightly narrower product columns.
